sphere_commentary.overview:
The three series show comparable average efficacy but divergent patterns in consistency and spread.
• HEALING demonstrates the highest consistency with low variance across protocols.
• THRIVING achieves the highest individual protocol means, particularly in Focus & Clarity.
• TRANSFORMING exhibits the greatest spread and lowest average scores, aligning with its ascending‑arc design for low‑affect states.
sphere_commentary.cross_series:
Protocol types (DESCENT, HOLD, ASCENT) show efficacy patterns matching their intended regulatory arcs.
• HEALING DESCENT protocols yield stable outcomes near 7.0, consistent with nervous‑system regulation.
• THRIVING HOLD protocols, especially Focus & Clarity, reach the highest means (up to 7.63) and show progressive gains at higher levels.
• TRANSFORMING ASCENT protocols, particularly in Motivation & Drive and Mood & Energy, deliver lower averages and higher variance, reflecting the challenge of entraining low‑affect states.
sphere_commentary.anomalies:
Several protocols show discrepancies between observed outcomes and qualitative reports, model predictions, or stability metrics.
• H-CR-L1 (n=43) – low mean (6.35) despite qualitative reports of significant improvement – suggests possible survey misalignment or listener state effects.
• T-FC-L3 (n=35) – high mean (7.63) with notable analytical drift and model prediction gap – warrants investigation into interpretation consistency.
• X-MD-L1 (n=22) – low positive rate (45%) and large AutoGluon-observed discrepancy (7.876 vs 6.36) – indicates potential population mismatch or design issue.
sphere_commentary.development_signals:
Several protocols show gaps between observed outcomes and model predictions or qualitative reports, suggesting refinement opportunities.
• H-CR-L1 (n=43) – low crisis DESCENT outcome – test shortening descent phase or adding adviser-guided hold for faster entrainment.
• T-FC-L3 (n=35) – high Focus & Clarity efficacy – explore L2 variant to scale successful elements or increase visibility in focus pathways.
• X-ME-L1 (n=39) – low-affect protocol underperforming relative to AutoGluon prediction (8.230 vs 6.74) – investigate population mismatch and consider increasing hold phase or adjusting rhythm density.
sphere_commentary.embedding_analysis:
Embedding analysis: Cross-run drift metrics indicate widespread analytic instability, though data limitations hinder clustering.
• CROSS‑RUN DRIFT: 23-29 of 30 protocols show similarity below 0.85 (per analyzer runs), with X‑MD‑L3 consistently lowest (~0.507).
• CROSS‑PROTOCOL SEMANTIC CLUSTERS: insufficient data for meaningful clustering across all analyzers.
• Confidence note: drift metrics are based on limited run history; interpretation should be cautious due to potential analytical instability.
